subject.title: feat(ios): Siri App Intent integration — native "Hey Siri, ask OpenClaw..." support

question: Should native Siri/App Intent support send agent requests through the paired iOS node identity, through a hardened /hooks/agent-style token boundary, or stay out of core for now?
rationale: Current main has both paired-node chat/node-event paths and token-gated hook paths, and the correct boundary affects credentials, local confirmation, session state, and whether OS automations may trigger agent work.

options.title: Use paired-node identity
options.body: Build the intent around the existing authenticated iOS node/operator session and chat.send or node.event semantics, with explicit local confirmation and session routing.

options.title: Use hardened hook boundary
options.body: Allow the Siri intent to call a hook-like boundary only after maintainers define token storage, session-key allowlisting, reply collection, and automation permissions.

options.title: Defer native Siri support
options.body: Keep Shortcuts/webhook or Talk Mode workarounds until iOS voice-entry product direction is clearer.

recommendation.title: Use paired-node identity
recommendation.body: Build the intent around the existing authenticated iOS node/operator session and chat.send or node.event semantics, with explicit local confirmation and session routing.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely decision spans iOS AppIntents, Talk Mode, Gateway chat transport, and security defaults where steipete has the strongest feature-history signal.
